subject: OrbitPay — VPC boundary & data retention follow-up
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@orbitpay.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@orbitpay.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 18:20:00 +0000
Subject: OrbitPay discovery - network & retention items (recap + asks)

Hi Priya + Marcus,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful. Putting a short recap and the open questions so we have a single reference. I've attached a rough network diagram (orbitpay_network_outline.pdf) that shows where we expect Redwood to run (private VPC peering to our processing tier).

Key constraints / asks:
- PII boundary: Cardholder data and full payment tokens must never leave our private VPC. We need clarity on whether Redwood can ensure model inference happens entirely on the customer-managed subnet with no outbound egress to public endpoints.
- Logging: We require request/response audit logs for 180 days. Logs must capture request id, timestamp, model version, and a redacted request hash (no raw PII stored). Is that supported by Redwood Private?
- Data retention & deletion: For any cached prefixes/KV caches, we need control to purge within 24 hours on demand. We also need a formal retention policy we can include in our security questionnaire.
- Air-gap possibility: If the pilot goes well, we may require an air-gapped single-tenant deployment. Can you outline differences vs. standard Private (deploy/ops overhead, lead times)?
- Network egress: Any calls to telemetry, update checks, or model registries must be optional/off by default.

Would appreciate short bullet answers against each item. Evan and I will share this with our security team. Tentative timeline: pilot in July, production decision in Q4.

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
Head of Platform Security | OrbitPay
[sent attachment: orbitpay_network_outline.pdf]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@orbitpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 20:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: OrbitPay discovery - network & retention items (recap + asks)

Hi Sophie (and Evan),

Appreciate the clear write-up and the diagram — that helps a lot. Below are concise answers; Marcus and Tessa will follow with technical detail and a short matrix we can use in your questionnaire.

- PII boundary: Redwood Private supports deployment inside a customer-managed VPC. The inference runtime can be pinned to subnets that have no NAT gateway and only allow egress through customer-controlled endpoints (so no public internet egress unless you configure it). For the pilot we can provide a hardened config that prevents external DNS/HTTP egress.

- Logging: We can emit request-level audit events to your secure logging endpoint (syslog/HTTPS/S3) with configurable retention. By default Redwood keeps operational logs for 30 days; for your requirement we can configure a 180-day retention on logs forwarded to your storage. We do not persist raw request payloads in central logs unless explicitly configured.

- Data retention & purge: KV cache/prefix cache can be purged via an admin API call; we can expose a workflow for a 24-hour purge SLA during the pilot. We'll document the purge procedure and retention settings.

- Air-gap: We have an on-prem/air-gapped packaging option. The main differences: (1) deployment artifacts delivered as an offline bundle; (2) additional validation and longer prep time (~3-5 weeks) for image signing and air-gapped install; (3) limited remote support patterns — we rely more on orchestrated runbooks and staged deployments. We'll include an estimated timeline.

- Network egress: Telemetry and automatic model update checks are optional and disabled by default in Private. Any outbound endpoints are configurable and can be restricted to customer-managed proxies.

Next steps: Marcus will attach a short privacy matrix and a technical note on subnet configuration. Can you confirm the exact logging destination (S3 bucket or SIEM endpoint) and whether OrbitPay requires HSM-backed key storage for model encryption at rest?

I'll add these items to the HubSpot deal — HS-23451 — and propose a follow-up technical session next week (Marcus + Aditya + your infra lead).

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

[sent attachments: rdw_privacy_matrix.xlsx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@orbitpay.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 01:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: OrbitPay discovery - network & retention items (recap + asks)

Hi team,

Quick technical notes (high level) — happy to go deeper on the follow-up call:

1) VPC placement and egress controls:
   - Option A (tightest): Run inference in subnets with no route to IGW or NAT; only allow egress via VPC peering + customer proxy endpoints. No DNS resolution to public namespaces unless you host resolver in VPC.
   - Option B (managed): Allow outbound through customer NAT but lock down egress using security groups and proxy rules.
   - We can support both; Option A is the safer default for PII-sensitive traffic.

2) Caching behavior:
   - KV/prefix caches are bounded and can be configured per-model. Cache persistence is optional and lives on ephemeral volumes unless you opt-in to persistent caches.
   - Purge API: POST /admin/cache/purge?model=<id>&scope=all — will be documented in the runbook. We can instrument a 24-hr SLA for the pilot (manual trigger + confirmation).

3) Logs & Audit:
   - Audit payload includes: request_id, timestamp, model_name:version, response_size, inference_latency_ms. Raw prompt text will only be included if you enable prompt logging; otherwise we emit a prompt_hash.
   - For your 180-day requirement we recommend forwarding logs to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules you control.

4) Air-gapped deployment notes:
   - Deliverables: signed images, offline installer, runbook, customer-side verification checklist.
   - Support: we provide a runbook-based support bundle and an on-call window for cutover (limited remote diagnostics due to no outbound).

Attaching the privacy matrix we promised; it maps items to config knobs and docs. Happy to convert any row to the wording your security questionnaire needs.

- Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

[sent attachments: rdw_privacy_matrix.xlsx]

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@orbitpay.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@orbitpay.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: OrbitPay discovery - network & retention items (recap + asks)

Thanks — that all looks sensible and addresses most of our immediate concerns. A few clarifications before we lock the pilot: 

- Logging destination: S3 (s3://orbitpay-security-logs) with bucket policies controlled by our security team. We will provide a write-only IAM role for Redwood to deliver logs.
- HSM: For production we prefer HSM-backed keys for model encryption at rest; pilot can use KMS but please outline migration steps to HSM in the runbook.
- Pilot scope: We want a 2-week pilot ingesting synthetic (non-PII) traffic first, then a second 2-week window with tokenized (non-reversible) payment data. Can you confirm that sequence works operationally?

If all good, let's schedule the technical session for next Wednesday (21 Jul) at 14:00 PT — Marcus + Aditya + our infra lead. I will share the S3 info and the security questionnaire items in a follow-up email.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sophie
Head of Platform Security | OrbitPay
